messages:
jamal: quick recap — I ran a focused staging load run to help set sane defaults for RPM/TPM and our burst handling. Goal was to identify knee points for 429s and latency degradation for the Deploy API (text-generation endpoint). ran across two surprising things, posting raw results and repro steps below.

carmen: nice, thanks. which test harness did you use? k6/wrk?

jamal: k6. script ramp: 0 -> 150 VUs over 2m, hold 3m, ramp down. each VU issues requests at a fixed rate so we can control RPM/TM semantics. model=redwood-7b, seq=512 tokens avg. config snippet: ```javascript
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function () {
  const payload = JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-7b', prompt: 'Hello', max_tokens: 512 });
  const res = http.post('https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', payload, { headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer $TEST_KEY', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } });
  sleep(1);
}
```

sophia: did you saturate token throughput or request concurrency? those give very different failure modes.

jamal: both. we ran two variants: (A) fixed RPS with varying concurrency (simulate many small requests) and (B) fixed concurrency with large token responses (simulate long outputs). results: 
- Variant A: when per-key RPM > 600 we start seeing 429s with Retry-After ~ 10s, downstream tail latency spikes (95th from 120ms -> 950ms).
- Variant B: TPM limits kick earlier — around 720k tokens/min per key we see unfair queuing and 429s without proper Retry-After in some routed paths (bug?).

alice: can you paste an example 429 header you saw? we need to double-check our middleware sets X-RateLimit and Retry-After consistently.

jamal: yes — sample response headers captured: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 10
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1718201300
```
but in ~12% of 429s the Retry-After header was missing (looks like a routing fallback to the capacity-tier handler).

carmen: is that the handler that triggers when dedicated-pool capacity is exhausted and we fallback to best-effort? if so, we should add a guard to return consistent headers — ops-oncall, FYI.

ops-oncall: noted. raising a short PR to ensure the fallback path sets Retry-After + X-RateLimit-* today. also adding logs for which pool returned the 429.

sophia: what about burst window config? we currently have burst_size=2x, burst_window=10s (token-bucket). did tests show that is sufficient?

jamal: interestingly, 2x/10s is too permissive for some high-concurrency clients. with many concurrent keys we saw token storming where each key used its burst, causing aggregate pressure. suggestions: reduce per-key burst to 1.5x or keep 2x but cap global burst pool per account. numbers I recommend: per-key RPM default = 200, per-key TPM default = 120k, burst multiplier = 1.5, burst_window = 10s, burst_burst_duration hard cap 30s.

alice: can you share the raw k6 metrics (RPS, errors, p95 latency) so we can put into the PR? also need a simple repro curl so support can reproduce for escalations.

jamal: pasted summary metrics (from k6 summary): ```
scenarios: 2
requests: 43200
checks: 0
http_req_duration: { p(95)=0.95s, p(99)=1.8s }
http_req_failed: 5.2% (mainly 429s)
mean_data_received: 12.4 kB
mean_req_duration: 220 ms
```
repro curl (single thread high RPM): ```bash
for i in $(seq 1 800); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":64}' https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done; wait
```
this script pushed one key to ~480 RPM in ~60s and you can observe 429s start to appear.

carmen: thanks — that's actionable. we should add a small test suite in ci-load that runs the curl repro against a sandbox and ensures our defaults don't drop below N requests before 429 threshold. maybe assert no more than 1% 429 under 200 RPM/120k TPM.

sophia: agree. one more note — for TPM accounting we saw mismatch between token estimation vs actual tokens produced when model used sampling (longer outputs). need to ensure our TPM enforcement uses actual emitted tokens not requested max_tokens.

jamal: yep, observed that too. one last oddity — a small number of keys were allowed higher RPM by the routing policy (customer-tier=internal-beta) and those keys had their own dedicated pool; those pools handled bursts better but increased cross-pool pressure. proposal: default keep per-key conservative, and let dedicated pool configs override via explicit contract.

ops-oncall: created ticket INF-876 to: 1) patch fallback 429 headers; 2) add logs indicating pool; 3) add ci-load test for the repro script. assigning to @carmen for CI work, @alice for support doc, @sophia for TPM accounting change.

alice: I'll draft a support KB with the curl repro, expected headers, and guidance: "if customers hit 429s, check X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After; ask for a short traffic pattern sample and whether they hit bursts from many API keys."

sophia: I'll open a tiny PR to change TPM calc to use tokens_emitted rather than requested_max and add a dashboard to show tokens_emitted vs tokens_requested.

jamal: thanks folks. next steps: implement fixes, re-run the k6 suite, target new defaults opt-in for next staging roll. ping me when PRs are up so I can run a quick regression pass. :thumbsup: 

sre-bot: Created INF-876 and linked to this thread (priority: medium).
